title: Cavan Sullivan Injury: Progress, Potential Return Date for USMNT Wonderkid
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia VeselyOct 27, 2026Cavan Sullivan missed two consecutive matches due to injury. / Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesCavan Sullivan missed two consecutive MLS matches last week due to injury, putting worry into American fans just days away from the U.S. men’s national team’s November camp. However, it seems he is now firmly on the mend and could be healthy enough to feature in the nation’s competitive action later this month.

The 17-year-old winger was absent for two of the Philadelphia Union’s most intense matches this season, watching as his side fell 2–1 to the No. 2 ranked New England Revolution on Oct. 24 and draw 0–0 with Supporters’ Shield winners Nashville SC on Wednesday. Although the two results were still enough to punch their ticket to the postseason, the Union will be eager to see their brightest star return to full fitness as they attempt to make a deep run in the playoffs.

Sullivan has lit up MLS ever since interim manager Ryan Richter came in this summer and gave the teenager a real chance. Seven goals and 14 assists later, the youngster has proven himself as a legend in the making and the future of American soccer.

He beat out the likes of Lionel Messi for the MLS Player of the Month for September and even became the youngest USMNT goalscorer in history in his debut camp under manager Mauricio Pochettino earlier this month.

The teenager may be defying all odds, but he’s still a mere mortal. Richter will need him healthy for the Union’s playoff push, and Pochettino will need him at full strength in order to name him for the upcoming Concacaf Nations League matches.

Sullivan suffered an ankle injury on Oct. 17. /  Isaiah Vazquez/MLS/Getty ImagesSullivan suffered an ankle injury on Oct. 17 in the 2–2 draw with Charlotte FC. Although the fiery teenager managed to fight through the pain and see out all 90 minutes at Subaru Park, the injury kept him out for nearly two weeks afterward. He made his return to the pitch on Saturday afternoon, a brief display against FC Cincinnati.

Richter had only expected Sullivan to be out for a few days total, confident he would be available as early as the clash with the Revs. “He’s all good,” Richter said five days after the injury. “He took a knock in the game on Saturday against Charlotte, and we’re just trying to manage that through this week. But he should be available for Saturday [Oct. 24]. He was out on the field today, but like I said, just managing that through the week and trying to get him so that he’s at his best for this weekend.”

Sullivan, however, was listed unavailable by Friday evening, and the teenager was helpless as his team suffered its first loss in 16 league matches, snapping an undefeated streak that dated all the way back to May. He was once again listed as unavailable on Tuesday evening, benched for the bout in Nashville.

Sullivan helped the USMNT defeat bitter rival Mexico earlier this month. /  Kevin Abele/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesSullivan made a 30-minute cameo off the bench on Saturday afternoon at TQL Stadium, replacing forward Ezekiel Alladoh at the hour mark.

Although he failed to generate a goal contribution in the eventual 1–0 loss (a rarity for him these days), the youngster took no time at all getting involved in the Union’s threatening offensive antics, playing a part in three separate attempts to overcome Cincinnati’s late lead.

What remains to be seen is whether or not Pochettino will include him in his roster next week. The Stars and Stripes will convene on Nov. 9, ahead of two-consecutive matches against Haiti in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals, their first competitive fixtures since the 2026 World Cup.
Sullivan will be eager to continue making a name for himself on the global stage, and Pochettino will certainly want to discover if he really is the future of the USMNT.
